clue.text: Get away from test centre with carbon copy

indicators.note: the centre of the word test is its middle pair of letters

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
to ape is to copy or mimic

explanation.surface: An examinee flees an exam hall clutching a carbon duplicate of the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to break free or flee, a straight synonym of get away.

clue.text: Authentic quartet from Liechtenstein

indicators.note: a set of four letters is taken from inside the word Liechtenstein

explanation.surface: Something genuine, perhaps a string quartet, hails from the small Alpine principality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quartet from' says take a run of four letters out of Liechtenstein, here its second to fifth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German loanword in English meaning genuine or real, a synonym of authentic.

clue.text: Newspaper boss sent up after conspirator falls

indicators.note: after puts the editor piece behind the conspirator

parts.note: Casca is one of the conspirators who stab Caesar in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the letters are read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: An editor is ridiculed once a plotter takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reverses the editor in this down clue, and 'after' sets it behind Casca, the plotter from Shakespeare's Julius Caesar; 'falls' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, especially a series of small ones, so it means falls of water.

clue.text: Insect burrowing into straight banana

indicators.note: burrowing into says one piece goes inside the other, as a creature digs into fruit

parts.note: plain can mean straightforward, simple, direct: straight
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug tunnels into a perfectly ordinary banana.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a type of banana usually cooked before eating.

clue.text: I holler out loud for something to eat in parlour

indicators.note: out loud signals that the words are to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: holler means scream or shout, so I holler gives I scream

explanation.surface: Someone shouts loudly for a snack in an ice-cream parlour.
explanation.walkthrough: The old rhyme 'I scream, you scream, we all scream for ice cream' plays on the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice-cream parlour is a shop selling ice cream, the dessert eaten there.

clue.text: Senator's first to abandon a gun in cool part of Washington

indicators.note: in places the shortened gun inside the word for cool

parts.note: chill means cool

indicators.note: to abandon means that letter leaves the gun word

parts.note: a pistol is a gun

indicators.note: Senator's first means the opening letter of the word Senator

explanation.surface: A senator gives up carrying a weapon in a calm corner of Washington DC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' drops the senator's initial from the weapon, and 'in' sets what remains inside the word for cool, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitol Hill is the district of Washington DC where Congress meets.

clue.text: Fur is for mammals

parts.note: an animal's fur is its coat

explanation.surface: Fur is suitable for mammals, as a statement of nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Coatis are raccoon-like animals of the Americas, so they are mammals.

clue.text: Letter left in European skiing area

indicators.note: in places the left letter inside the ski run

parts.note: a piste is a prepared ski run

explanation.surface: A letter has been forgotten on a ski slope somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, as in the epistles of the New Testament.

clue.text: Married woman accepts grand new short wave generator

indicators.note: accepts means the married woman takes the other letters into herself

parts.note: a matron is a married woman, especially a dignified one
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: short means the word new loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A wife takes in a big new shortwave radio set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short wave' looks like one phrase but is split: 'short' trims the new, and 'accepts' tucks grand plus the trimmed word into the married woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetron is a valve generating microwaves, as in radar and microwave ovens.

clue.text: Turning without due care to capture American soldier

indicators.note: to capture means the turned word holds the American letters
Turning means the reckless word is read backwards

parts.note: rash means acting without due care

explanation.surface: A careless driver swerves to seize a US serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses the reckless word, and 'to capture' has it hold the American letters after its first letter; a hussar is a cavalryman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalry soldier.

clue.text: Conversing quietly in a helicopter

indicators.note: in places the quiet letter inside the helicopter's name

parts.note: the Sea King is a helicopter long used by the Royal Navy and RAF
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Two people talk in hushed tones aboard a chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking is talking, and conversing is talking with someone.

clue.text: Prickliest ground with that side?

indicators.note: ground, as in ground down or crushed, means the letters are broken and remade

explanation.surface: A thorny plant is crushed along with something else, the other side of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTICK THISTLE is a Scottish football club from Glasgow; 'side' is a team. 'ground' fits football as a stadium but here means crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a sports team, and this is a Glasgow football club.

clue.text: Tory pamphlet — one about Labour movement

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory
a tract is a short pamphlet
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A Conservative leaflet with one item on the trade-union movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour movement' looks political but means childbirth labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraction is a tightening of the womb during labour in childbirth.

clue.text: Toed line by yielding thus?

indicators.note: yielding means giving way, so the letters of these words give way and reform

explanation.surface: Someone who toed the line by giving way did so dutifully.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: toeing the line by yielding is acting dutifully.
explanation.definitionFit: Toeing the line and yielding to authority describe acting in a compliant, dutiful manner.

clue.text: Obscure cafe — but so original

indicators.note: original, as in inventive, asks for a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A little-known café that is nonetheless very original.
explanation.definitionFit: To obfuscate is to make unclear, so it means to obscure as a verb.

clue.text: Expensive honey

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment, like darling

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both costly and a beloved person addressed fondly.

clue.text: Gelatinous substance from a fish that's been cloned

indicators.note: something cloned is copied exactly, so the piece appears twice

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A jelly-like substance is taken from a fish that has been genetically duplicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar-agar is a jelly made from seaweed, used in cooking and laboratories.

clue.text: They serve older boys cigarettes

definitions.meaning: at British public schools, younger pupils who did chores for senior boys

explanation.walkthrough: At traditional British boarding schools, junior boys were made to run errands for seniors, a practice called fagging.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the word means junior schoolboys acting as servants, and slang cigarettes.

clue.text: Welcome event not expected in Götterdämmerung?

definitions.meaning: a stroke of unexpected good fortune
Wagner's opera title means twilight of the gods, so its subject is the deities' finish

explanation.walkthrough: Götterdämmerung, the last opera of Wagner's Ring cycle, depicts the downfall of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is a welcome surprise; split, it reads as the end of the gods.

clue.text: Seeing how far one can go in fitting room?

definitions.text: Seeing how far one can go
definitions.meaning: pushing one's luck to test limits
what a shopper does with clothes in a changing cubicle

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means testing limits, and literally describes putting on clothes before buying.

clue.text: Young swimmer needing little support

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
a pole is a support

explanation.surface: A young swimmer needs a bit of backing from the coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a frog's or toad's larva, a young creature that swims.

clue.text: Home help for a posh couple?

parts.note: U means upper-class, the British term for posh
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A domestic helper hired by a well-to-do couple.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreigner living with a family and helping in the home.

clue.text: Salt that may be extracted from china clay?

definitions.text: Salt that may be extracted from china clay?

parts.words: Salt that may be extracted from china clay?
parts.note: the chemical formula NaCl sits hidden in the letters of chiNA CLay

explanation.walkthrough: Chemistry gives the formula NaCl, which appears literally in 'chiNA CLay'; china clay itself is kaolin, not salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Common table salt is the compound of sodium and chlorine, formula NaCl.

clue.text: Introductions to major essayists: Addison, Thoreau, Bacon and Lamb?

indicators.note: introductions means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A survey of great essayists from Addison and Thoreau to Bacon and Lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Bacon and Charles Lamb were essayists too, but here bacon and lamb are foods.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon and lamb are both kinds of animal flesh eaten as food.

clue.text: A very English mass — with song and prayer

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass in physics
an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: A thoroughly English mass featuring music and prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ave Maria, or Hail Mary, is a Catholic prayer to the Virgin.

clue.text: Pay no attention to rocky region

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaky, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Disregard the stony district.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to disregard it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: First signs of Eurasian nuthatch in evergreen

indicators.note: first signs means the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: during means in, as in during the night

explanation.surface: Early sightings of a Eurasian bird among the pine trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evergreen' looks like a tree but is the adjective meaning lasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen, used figuratively, means perennially popular or lasting.

clue.text: Silver paper finally swallowed by spy

indicators.note: swallowed by means the spy takes the letter inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word paper

explanation.surface: A secret agent eats the end of a document to destroy evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: ARGENT is the heraldic term for silver.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry argent is the tincture silver, from the Latin for silver.
